name: code-review-v2
frozen: before any paid call; see RULE.md

cases.rationale: startswith on a path without a trailing separator: ../files_secret/x resolves to /srv/files_secret/x, which passes; abspath doesn't resolve symlinks either
realpath resolves .. and symlinks; commonpath compares whole path components, so only paths inside BASE pass

cases.target:
Python:
def last_commit(ref):
    # ref comes from the query string
    r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "log", "-n1", ref], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
cases.rationale: no shell, but ref can be an option: --output=/var/www/x.php makes git log write a file of the attacker's choosing

cases.target:
Python:
def last_commit(ref):
    # ref comes from the query string
    r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "log", "-n1", "--end-of-options", ref], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
cases.rationale: --end-of-options (git 2.24+) makes ref a revision, never an option; reading any revision of this repo is intended
//evil.example starts with '/' but browsers treat it as a scheme-relative URL to another host
only a single leading slash followed by path-safe characters passes: no '//', backslash, tab or other control characters, so the browser can't read it as another host

cases.target:
Python:
def is_staff(email):
    # email comes from a public sign-up form
    return re.fullmatch(r"(\w+\s?)+@example\.com", email) is not None
cases.rationale: nested quantifier (\w+\s?)+ backtracks exponentially on input like 'aaaa...a!'

cases.target:
Python:
def is_staff(email):
    # email comes from a public sign-up form
    return re.fullmatch(r"[\w.+-]+@example\.com", email) is not None
cases.rationale: single character class with one quantifier: linear-time matching
JSON.parse makes __proto__ an own key; merge then writes through Object.prototype

__proto__ is skipped and recursion only enters the target's own properties, so inherited objects (Object.prototype, Object.prototype.toString) are never written; constructor/prototype keys just become plain own properties

cases.target:
Python 3.11:
def unpack(upload, dest):
    # upload is a user-supplied .tar file
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=upload) as t:
        t.extractall(dest)
cases.rationale: tarfile.extractall without a filter follows ../ and absolute member names and links (CVE-2007-4559)

cases.target:
Python 3.12:
def unpack(upload, dest):
    # upload is a user-supplied .tar file
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=upload) as t:
        t.extractall(dest, filter="data")
cases.rationale: the 'data' extraction filter rejects absolute paths, .. components, links outside dest and special files
every key in the request body is written, so a user can set is_admin

cases.target:
Python:
def check(request):
    sent = request.headers.get("X-Api-Token", "")
    return sent == os.environ["API_TOKEN"]
cases.rationale: == returns at the first differing byte, leaking how much of the token matched
constant-time comparison
random is a Mersenne Twister PRNG; its outputs are predictable, unfit for password-reset tokens
secrets uses the OS CSPRNG
the check only requires 'name' or 'email' somewhere in the string: 'name; DROP TABLE users' passes
only the two literal column names can reach the query
f-string SQL, but sort can only be name or email in some letter case, which SQL treats as the same column
